Tests.Name: .NET 10: Generic OrderedDictionary<TKey, TValue> Collection
Tests.Prompt:

MANDATORY REQUIREMENTS:
1. Explain the native generic 'System.Collections.Generic.OrderedDictionary<TKey, TValue>' introduced in .NET 9/10, explaining its O(1) key lookups, deterministic insertion order preservation, and indexed access.
2. Write a concise code example directly instantiating and consuming the built-in 'OrderedDictionary<string, int>' (demonstrating addition, access by key, and positional access by index). Do NOT implement a custom collection class from scratch.

Criteria.Description: Explains that .NET natively provides generic System.Collections.Generic.OrderedDictionary<TKey, TValue>, highlighting O(1) lookups, insertion-order preservation, and indexed access without requiring custom wrappers
Demonstrates instantiation and usage of built-in OrderedDictionary<TKey, TValue> showing both key-based lookup and positional index access without writing a custom dictionary class
